results.title: What You Need to Know About Reciprocal Tariffs [UPDATED] | Miller & Chevalier
results.content: On April 29, 2025, the president issued an executive order that revises how certain tariffs interact and "stack." While not impacting Reciprocal Tariffs, this order changes whether Section 232 automotive tariffs, Section 232 steel and aluminum tariffs, and IEEPA tariffs on products of Canada and Mexico remain cumulative. This amendment was made retroactive to entries made on or after March 4, 2025. Corrections to past entries must be submitted no later than 12:01 a.m. EDT on May 16, 2025. [...] Tariff. For example, even though products that are subject to Section 232 automotive tariffs are exempt from the Reciprocal Tariff, an automotive product will still be subject to the Reciprocal Tariff if zero percent automotive tariffs are owed. Consider an electrical rangefinder that is classified in HTS 9015.10, which could be used in automobiles to detect and measure the car's distance from an object or could be used in non-automotive contexts. Even though HTS 9015.10 is included in the list [...] in the list of HTS codes covered by the Section 232 automotive parts tariff, if the electrical rangefinder is not for use in a passenger vehicle or light truck, it is not subject to the Section 232 automotive tariff. As such, that electrical rangefinder will still be subject to the Reciprocal Tariff.

results.content:
According to the proclamation, goods qualifying for the USMCA will be exempt from the new Section 122 tariff, as will all products currently subject to Section 232 tariffs or those that may become subject to such tariffs in the future. Exemptions granted under the reciprocal tariffs recently struck down by the Supreme Court will also be preserved under the Section 122 tariff, including certain agricultural products, pharmaceuticals, electronics, passenger vehicles and trucks, aerospace [...] Exemptions preserved: USMCA qualifying goods; textiles/apparel under CAFTADR; all items covered by Section 232 tariffs (no stacking); and product specific carveouts that mirror the reciprocal tariff Annex (e.g., specified agricultural goods, pharmaceuticals/APIs, certain electronics, defined vehicle/parts sets, aerospace, and information materials)—as listed in the new Section 122 Annex.
